content:
Harry Potter fans have been given a first sample of Hans Zimmer's new HBO series soundtrack, and have complained that it doesn't yet compare to John Williams' beloved movie score.

Whether you like Harry Potter or not, you will know Hedwig's Theme — the iconic Harry Potter tune penned by legendary composer John Williams which stands alongside the very best of his other creations (Star Wars, Superman, Indiana Jones, and Jaws, to name but a few).

Despite being a hugely accomplished composer himself, Zimmer has a tough act to follow, then — and a first sampling of his new soundtrack for HBO's upcoming Harry Potter series does not seem to be doing him any favors.

This track comes from an official clip from the show released by HBO via YouTube which itself met with a decidedly mixed reaction. The scene — which features the start of term banquet — was criticized for its visuals, though there is significant debate online over whether the colorization of the scene has been properly represented. (Earlier peeks at the series were also thought to be washed out compared to the more colourful pallete used in the films.)

Zimmer's sountrack has also come under fire, with unfavourable comments on social media comparing the music to a "Simpsons Hit & Run theme," "those goofy ass copyright free YouTube songs," "if The Sims 1 had a Harry Potter expansion pack," and "Danny Elfman slop." Fans have now extracted the music from the clip and cleared it up for better listening, which you can hear above.

To be fair to Zimmer, this isn't designed to be the series' main theme or anything other than some light-hearted background music while Harry and Ron stuff their faces with roast chicken and cake. But as the first bit of music from the series to be released, fans are inevitably drawing conclusions about the rest of the soundtrack.

Zimmer's involvement in the series was announced earlier this year, when it was confirmed that the composer of Interstellar, The Dark Knight Trilogy, Gladiator and countless other blockbusters would be working with Kara Talve and Anže Rozman from Bleeding Fingers Music, an Emmy Award-winning collective of muscians he co-founded, to produce the new series' score.

"The musical legacy of Harry Potter is a touch point for composers everywhere and we are humbled to join such a remarkable team on a project of this magnitude," Zimmer said at the time. "The responsibility is something that myself, Kara Talve and Anže Rozman do not take lightly. Magic is all around us, often just beyond reach, but as in the world of Harry Potter, you simply must look for it. With this score we hope to bring audiences that little bit closer to it whilst honoring what has come before."

Just over a month remains until HBO debuts the first episode of its Harry Potter series on December 25, with episodes then following regularly into early 2027. Last month brought a fresh wave of casting confirmations, including Shameless and Fargo actor William H. Macy as the Sorting Hat.
